---
title: "Genomes and variants"
---

This page is about DNA itself: sequences, small differences between them, and family trees of organisms. In a note you can work with sequences and trees, and follow single strains of bacteria with marker genes.

## Prompts to try

Copy a prompt into a new note and send it. When the result is back, send the follow-up.

1. Find the germ behind an outbreak. Send:

   ```text
   Load LomanNJ_2013 from curatedMetagenomicData. It is stool from patients in the 2011 German Shiga-toxigenic E. coli outbreak.
   ```

   Then:

   ```text
   How abundant is Escherichia coli in each sample, and does it track the recorded count and ELISA result?
   ```

2. Follow donor strains after a faecal transplant:

   ```text
   Load LiSS_2016 from curatedMetagenomicData as species and as marker abundances. Men with metabolic syndrome received a faecal transplant and were followed to day 84.
   ```

3. Do babies share exact sequences with their own mothers?

   ```text
   Load SprockettTHData from microbiomeDataSets. The Dyad column links Tsimane mothers and infants. How many dyads have faeces from both mother and infant?
   ```

4. Start from DADA2 output:

   ```text
   Download Zenodo record 15490674. It has a DADA2 sequence table and taxonomy as RDS files, from stream water at 23 NEON sites.
   ```

## What a note can do

- **Sequences.** Biostrings reads and handles DNA sequences. DADA2 works with exact sequence variants (ASVs), the unique sequences found in amplicon data.
- **Trees.** MAFFT lines up sequences (through ips), and phangorn or IQ-TREE build a family tree from them. ape draws and handles trees.
- **Trees in microbiome data.** Use a tree for phylogenetic diversity and UniFrac, two measures that count how related the microbes are.
- **Strains.** curatedMetagenomicData has marker gene abundances and presence for each sample, so you can follow a strain, not only a species.

Work that starts from raw reads, such as assembling genomes or calling variants, runs in [Reports on Roihu](../start/reports-roihu.qmd#bio-tools). There, an agent works in your own project with the cores, memory and time you choose, and can use CSC tools such as bwa, SPAdes, Prokka, bcftools, GATK and PLINK.

## Example notes

- [Finding the pathogen in an outbreak](https://omicsbase.utu.fi/share/rGHc4sGVHjFZwWjJBK_IL): E. coli levels against the clinical tests.
- [Does a transplanted community stay? Markers after FMT](https://omicsbase.utu.fi/share/QGl_5yV555vspbduImV-D): donor strains followed in recipients for three months.
- [Fusobacterium in cancer stool at marker level](https://omicsbase.utu.fi/share/8mW2lfuQPnx5PxTf9KkCp): from one species to the marker genes behind it.
- [Do infants share ASVs with their own mothers?](https://omicsbase.utu.fi/share/WoTodZ_4maNe454C5JNuE): exact sequences shared within families, compared with strangers.
- [Zenodo: from DADA2 output to a TreeSE in NEON streams](https://omicsbase.utu.fi/share/ioEZ4A9i1dwzPxRhhiCqD): a DADA2 table with its sequences, made ready for analysis.
- [What does UniFrac measure?](https://omicsbase.utu.fi/share/-Y0tUO_KappuVkocspSoF): a tree-based distance on three small samples.
